The GB notification service prototype (GOV.UK Prototype Kit, Nunjucks views, one Express router) at ~/git/defra/defra-design/GB-notification-service, commit 04a073b (the checkout's HEAD is 04a073b, so files can be read in place; use git show 04a073b:<path> if it has moved). Design Release 2.1 is not a separate app: app/lib/design-release-2.1-version.js (42 lines) calls app/lib/version-mount.js (363 lines), which copies every route in app/routes.js under /design-release-2.1, keeps a separate session nest (_designRelease21, flag _isDesignRelease21Version), prefixes journey paths in redirects and render data, sets service-navigation hrefs, and renders app/views/design-release-2.1/<view>.html where one exists, otherwise the root view. app/routes.js is 13,114 lines: lines 1-11104 are about 510 helper functions (session, validation, view models, render functions), lines 11105-13102 are about 90 route handlers, lines 13103-13114 mount the versions (DR2.1 before DR2). Handlers branch on isDesignRelease21SessionData and isDesignRelease2SessionData; DR2.1 also sets isDesignRelease2Version, so both DR2 and DR2.1 branches apply under /design-release-2.1. Views in scope: the 39 DR2.1 overrides in app/views/design-release-2.1/ (about 4,500 lines), the 15 DR2.1 partials in app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/ (about 900 lines), the root views DR2.1 falls back on (address-book, address-book-add, address-book-add-usage, address-book-lookup, address-book-view, index; about 880 lines), the root partials the DR2.1 pages include or routes.js renders (notification-status, region-of-origin-code-input, arrival-date-picker, animal-identification-saved-animals, cph-number-input, permanent-address-new-address-fields, the four reason-for-import selects, transporter fields and banner, address-book-manual-address-fields), partials/design-release-2/cancel-amend-modal.html (included by layouts/journey.html), and layouts/main.html and layouts/journey.html. app/data/ holds 34 list files (about 3,900 lines) that routes.js requires. Cut into 16 parts by what a user sees: the shell and journey control, then the journey in page order (start, consignment, reason, identification, arrival and transit, transporter, roles and addresses, CPH and permanent address, documents, review and submit), then notification hub with amend and copy, dashboard, templates, and the address book in two parts. routes.js is too big for one agent, so each part reads the routes.js line ranges that hold its pages' helpers, render functions and handlers; the ranges tile lines 1-13114 with no gaps or overlaps, and a view or partial shared by two parts is read by both but claimed only for the pages the part names. Left out by scope: app/views/intro/ and intro/routes.js, app/views/design-release-2/ and app/views/partials/design-release-2/ (except the one modal journey.html includes), app/views/testing/ and app/lib/testing-version.js and design-release-2-version.js, and the root journey views that DR2.1 overrides. Also left out: app/assets/ (client-side JavaScript and Sass, not named by the scope; the rendered traces source covers client behaviour), and three files nothing in scope reads (app/data/package-types.js, app/data/place-of-origin-addresses.js, app/utils/notification-reference.js, used only by intro/routes.js or not at all).

claims.statement: Design release 2.1 is served under the base path /design-release-2.1.

Every route of the root router is copied under /design-release-2.1 (each method of each route, with the same handlers), so DR2.1 has the same pages and handlers as the root journey rather than its own route table.
The versions are mounted in the order testing, design release 2.1, design release 2; 2.1 is mounted before 2 so that /design-release-2.1 is not taken as a /design-release-2 path.

Under /design-release-2.1 the session data a page sees is a separate nest stored under the session key _designRelease21, so DR2.1 notifications, drafts and answers are kept apart from the root journey and the other versions.
Inside the DR2.1 session nest the flag _isDesignRelease21Version is set to true on every request, which handlers use to tell they are running as DR2.1.

Two session keys are shared across all versions rather than kept in the DR2.1 nest: the addresses added to the address book (addressBookAddedAddresses) and the submitted notifications (submittedNotifications). Reading or writing them in DR2.1 reads or writes the shared value.

When a DR2.1 request carries a form or query field (not starting with an underscore, not the session key and not a shared key) whose name also exists in the shared session outside the DR2.1 nest, the nest takes the outer session's value for that key before the handler runs.
claims.note: This copies the outer session's value into the nest; the posted value itself is applied later by the prototype kit. Recorded as observed, not interpreted further.

claims.statement: Before a DR2.1 response redirects or ends, the session is restored so the DR2.1 nest is saved back under _designRelease21 in the full session.

In DR2.1, a redirect to a journey path is prefixed with /design-release-2.1 (for example a redirect to /notification-hub goes to /design-release-2.1/notification-hub), and a redirect to / goes to /design-release-2.1.

In DR2.1, every string in the data passed to a page render that is a journey path is prefixed with /design-release-2.1, so links, form actions and back links built by handlers stay inside the version.

The journey path prefixes that are kept inside the version are: /create-notification, /notification-type, /origin-of-the-import, /what-are-you-importing, /reason-for-import, /consignment-details, /animal-identification-details, /additional-animal-details, /arrival-details, /transit-countries, /transporter, /upload-documents, /roles-and-addresses, /place-of-origin, /consignor-or-exporter, /consignee, /importer, /place-of-destination, /cph-number, /permanent-address, /contact-address-for-consignment, /review-notification, /declaration, /notification-submitted, /notification-hub, /notifications, /dashboard, /live-animals, /germinal-products, /templates, /actions, /changes, /inspection and /prototype/reason-for-import (each path itself or anything below it).
Paths that are not journey paths are left unprefixed: external or protocol-relative links, links not starting with /, fragment links starting with #, and any path not in the journey prefix list.

The address book (/address-book and anything below it), static assets (/public/, /plugin-assets/), the prototype kit management pages (/manage-prototype) and the service index (/index) are shared paths that are never prefixed with the version base path.

claims.statement: A page is treated as reached from the notification overview (hub) when its query or form carries from=hub.
A page is treated as reached from the check-your-answers review page when its query or form carries from=review.
A page is treated as reached from a template review when its query or form carries from=template-review, or the session is marked as editing a template from its review.

The return path to a template review is /templates/<template id> (the template being edited, or the session's template), or /templates when there is no template id; in DR2.1 this becomes /design-release-2.1/templates/<id>.

Saving a page while editing a template from its review saves the template, sets the success message "<template title> has been updated" (or "Template has been updated" when it has no title or name), clears the template editing state and returns to that template's review page.

A journey page's back link goes to the template review when the page was reached from a template review, to the notification overview (/notification-hub) when reached from the hub, and otherwise to the previous page in the journey.

A page reached from the check-your-answers review page does not get a back link to the review: the back-link rule only special-cases template review and hub, so from=review pages fall back to the previous journey page.
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of an isFromReview branch in getJourneyBackLink; individual pages may override their own back link.

claims.statement: The journey step order starts with origin of the import, what are you importing, reason for import and consignment details, in that order.
The animal identification details step follows consignment details only when at least one selected species has identifier fields.
The additional animal details step comes next only when that page would ask the certification purpose question or the unweaned animals question.
Arrival details is always a step, after the animal steps.
The transit countries step follows arrival details only when the means of transport is Rail or Road.
Means of transport values are normalised before the transit check: airplane and air mean Air; railway and rail mean Rail; road vehicle and road mean Road; vessel and sea mean Sea.

Roles and addresses, contact address for consignment and review notification are always steps, in that order, after documents.
In DR2.1, the declaration step after review is skipped when the user is creating a template; otherwise declaration is the last step.

The step order has no step for CPH number, permanent address, place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer or place of destination; those pages are reached from within roles and addresses or the hub, not as linear steps.

claims.statement: The next page after a step is the following step in the order; after the last step, or from a page that is not a step, the next page is the notification overview (/notification-hub) unless the caller gives another fallback.
After roles and addresses, the next page is the notification overview instead of contact address for consignment when every notification hub section is already complete.
A notification is being amended when its status is exactly Amend.
Journey forms send the button pressed as the action field; hub and review are soft-save actions (save and leave the linear flow), and continue moves on.

When a journey page is saved, the notification is persisted as a draft; then the action review goes to the review page (/review-notification), the action hub goes to the notification overview (/notification-hub), and any other action goes to the next page.
When a journey page is saved while editing a template from its review, the save returns to the template review and does not persist a draft notification.

When a section page continues, it returns to the template review if reached from one, to the notification overview if reached from the hub, to the review page if reached from review, and otherwise to the next page in the journey; the template review takes precedence over hub, and hub over review.

By default a DR2.1 journey page shows a primary "Save and continue" button (action continue), a secondary "Save and return to overview" button (action hub) and a "Cancel and return to overview" link to the notification overview (/design-release-2.1/notification-hub).
A page may change the default actions: rename any of the three, hide the save and return to overview button, hide the cancel link, or point the cancel link elsewhere.

claims.statement: GET /create-notification clears the current notification journey from the session but keeps the address book additions, draft notifications, deleted notification references, submitted notifications, saved templates, deleted template ids and the per-version session nests.
GET /create-notification also clears any in-progress template creation flag.
In Design Release 2.1, GET /create-notification with no category in the query string sends the user to the notification type page (/notification-type).

GET /create-notification with a recognised category query (for example from a category dashboard) skips the notification type page: it records that the journey started from a category dashboard, starts the notification with that type, and sends the user straight to /origin-of-the-import.

Starting a notification sets its type, sets its status to Draft, clears the template-creation flag, gives it a new notification reference (in the design releases) and saves it as a draft notification.
claims.quote:
sessionData.notificationType = notificationType
  sessionData.notificationStatus = 'Draft'
  delete sessionData.isCreatingTemplate

  if (isDesignRelease2SessionData(sessionData)) {
    sessionData.notificationReference = generateDesignReleaseNotificationReference(sessionData)
  }

  persistDraftNotification(sessionData)

claims.statement: The notification type page pre-selects the type already held for the notification.

When no type is stored, the notification's type is worked out from its selections: germinal products only means germinal products, and selected species that are all live-animal species means live animals; otherwise the type is empty.

The server accepts a notification type given either as its value or as its display label (case-insensitive), and also recognises three types the page does not offer: products of animal origin or animal by-products, high-risk food or feed of non-animal origin, and plants, plant products or other objects.

Choosing a notification type marks the journey as not started from a category dashboard.
Changing the notification type to a different one from before clears every selected commodity and species.
When creating a template, choosing a notification type stores the type, sets the status to Draft and sends the user to /templates/create instead of the origin page.

Choosing a notification type starts a new notification (reference, Draft status, saved draft) when there is no notification reference yet; when there is one, it updates the type and saves the draft again.
After a valid notification type is chosen, every type (including plants for planting, potatoes and wood products) goes on to /origin-of-the-import.

claims.statement: Copy as new is reached at GET /notifications/copy-as-new; outside a Design Release 2 or 2.1 session it redirects to /.
Copy as new and amend with ?submitted=<id> use that submitted notification's saved snapshot; if no submitted notification has that id, the user is sent back to the dashboard.

Copy as new and amend with ?reference=<reference> use that dashboard notification's saved snapshot, or build one from its dashboard details when it has none; if the reference is not found, the user is sent back to the dashboard.
Copy as new and amend with neither ?submitted nor ?reference use the notification currently in the session.
'Back to the dashboard' from these routes means the design release's own dashboard path (such as /design-release-2.1), or / when there is none.

Copy as new starts a fresh notification: it clears the journey, keeping only the user's address book additions, drafts, submitted notifications, deleted references, saved and deleted templates and the version flags.
Copy as new carries over the import details: country of origin, whether a region of origin is required, the region of origin code and its suffix, and the internal reference.
Copy as new carries over what is being imported: the selected species, commodity selections, commodity id, code and name, and the notification type.

Copy as new carries over the main reason for import and its follow-ups: import reason, internal market purpose, transhipment destination country, transit exit border control post, transit destination country, temporary admission exit date and temporary admission port of exit.
Copy as new carries over the additional animal details: certification purpose, unweaned animals and storage temperature.

Copy as new carries over the roles and addresses: place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination addresses (with their ids), the CPH number, and the permanent address details (address, id, same-as-destination answer, summary and animals).

Copy as new does not carry over the shipment-specific details: the number of animals, packages and net weight, animal identifiers, port of entry, arrival date, transport, transit countries, transporter, uploaded documents or the contact address. The user enters these again.
claims.note: Inferred from what the carried-over list leaves out, compared with the fields a snapshot holds (for example dashboard-notification-snapshots.js:62-97 and 159-172).

claims.statement: Only fields that have a value in the source are copied; each copied value is a deep copy, so changing the new notification does not change the original.

When copying, an older certification purpose is mapped to a current option: 'Breeding' and 'Breeding and/or production' become 'Further keeping', 'Slaughter' stays 'Slaughter', and any other value not in the current options becomes 'Further keeping'.
If the copied notification has no notification type, it is worked out from the copied answers.
The copy gets a new notification reference and the status 'Draft', with no errors.
The copy is saved as a draft straight away, before the user changes anything.
After copying, the user is taken to the notification hub.
Amend is reached at GET /notifications/amend; outside a Design Release 2 or 2.1 session it redirects to /, and when the notification cannot be found it sends the user back to the dashboard.

Amend loads the whole saved notification into the session, replacing the current journey answers but keeping the drafts, submitted notifications, deleted references, address book additions and version flags.
claims.note: Unlike resetNotificationJourneySession, this list does not keep savedTemplates or deletedTemplateIds, so loading a snapshot for amend may drop saved templates unless the snapshot carries them.

claims.statement: An amended notification keeps its original reference: the snapshot's reference, else the ?reference value, else a newly generated one.
While amending, the notification's status is 'Amend'.
Amend records which notification is being amended, by submitted id and by reference, so that submitting replaces it and cancelling returns to it.
Amend keeps a copy of the notification as it was before the amendment, for change detection, and clears any errors.
After choosing to amend, the user is taken to the review page of the notification.
A notification counts as changed during an amendment when its answers differ from the copy taken when the amendment started; with no copy taken it never counts as changed.

Change detection ignores everything that is not a notification answer: errors, messages, the commodity search box, the status, the amend bookkeeping, version flags, drafts, submitted notifications, saved templates, deleted references and address book additions.
What the page does with the amend change check (for example, whether submitting an unchanged amendment is blocked) is not in this slice.
claims.note: hasAmendChanges is defined here but called from the review and submit handlers, which other parts own.

claims.statement: Cancel amend is reached at GET /notifications/cancel-amend; outside a Design Release 2 or 2.1 session it redirects to /.
Cancelling an amendment clears the amend bookkeeping, the original copy, the 'Amend' status and any errors.
claims.quote:
delete req.session.data.amendingFrom
  delete req.session.data.amendOriginalSnapshot
  delete req.session.data.notificationStatus

claims.statement: After cancelling an amendment, the user goes back to the submitted notification's review page (by submitted id when known, otherwise by reference), or to the dashboard when neither is known.
Cancelling an amendment does not write anything back to the submitted notification: edits made during the amendment are left in the session and are not saved over the submitted record.
claims.note: Inferred: the handler only clears state and redirects; submitted records change only in saveSubmittedNotification. The review page reloads the submitted record by id or reference.

claims.statement: A notification is saved as a draft automatically only in a Design Release 2 or 2.1 session, and never while a template is being created or a notification is being amended.
A draft is only saved when the notification has a reference; before saving, a missing or malformed reference is replaced with a generated one.
There is one draft per reference: saving replaces any existing draft with the same reference, moves it to the top of the drafts list and keeps its original created date.

A saved draft records the commodity codes, commodity names, a category of 'Germinal products' or 'Live animals', the country of origin (or 'Not applicable'), the arrival date formatted for the dashboard, the status 'Draft', and the full notification.
A saved draft or submitted notification has a quantity labelled 'Number of packages' (germinal products only) or 'Number of animals', whose value is the total, or empty when the total is zero.
claims.quote: quantityLabel: hasGerminalProductsOnly(snapshot) ? 'Number of packages' : 'Number of animals',

claims.statement: Submitting an amendment replaces the original submitted notification (matched by submitted id or reference) and keeps its id; a new submission is added to the top of the submitted list with a new id.
A submitted notification's status is 'Submitted action required' with an orange tag when any conditional submission items are outstanding, otherwise 'Submitted' with a green tag.

A submitted notification records the same dashboard details as a draft (reference, commodities, category, quantity, origin, arrival date), the submitted time and the full notification; its reference falls back to the default reference.
Submitting a notification removes its draft (the draft with the same reference).
Submitting ends any amendment: the amend bookkeeping, the original copy and the status are cleared.
claims.quote:
delete sessionData.amendingFrom
  delete sessionData.amendOriginalSnapshot
  delete sessionData.notificationStatus

claims.statement: Deleting a notification removes it from the session's submitted notifications (by id or by reference) and its drafts (by reference), and records the reference as deleted so a seeded notification with that reference no longer shows on any dashboard list.
A card in the error variant (action required or delayed) carries a red marker and shows its error message under the header.

The card's second row shows the quantity ('Number of animals' or 'Number of packages'), 'Origin', 'Consignor' and, when inspection is required, an 'Inspection' field with a 'Required' tag.
The card shows the arrival date as dd/mm/yyyy with leading zeros, the stored text where it cannot be read as a date, and 'Not applicable' when there is none.

A journey section can start an address book add with /address-book/add?from=<section id>: for a selectable consignment address section it records where to return and suggests that section's address type, then goes to /address-book/add/lookup.

The journey sections that suggest an address type are place of origin (Place of origin), consignor or exporter (Consignor), consignee (Consignee), importer (Importer) and place of destination (Place of destination).
The contact address can start an address book add with /address-book/add?from=contact-address, which records a return to the contact address and goes to the add-details step.
When the add started from a journey section and one of the ticked types matches that section, the new address becomes that section's selected address.
When the add started from a journey section, saving returns the user to that section's page with the '<name> address added to your address book' message shown there instead of in the address book.
When the add started from the contact address, saving also adds it to the contact addresses, selects it as the contact address and returns the user there with the success message.

An add started from a journey section or the contact address sets no address book category, so under DR2.1 it shows the root 'Add address details' lookup page rather than the DR2.1 'Add address and contact details' page.
claims.note: Inferred: the from paths set addressBookAddressType but not addressBookAddressCategory, and only a usage category routes to the DR2.1 page. A stale category left in session from an earlier add would change this.
